net sales.heading: Revenue Recognition
net sales.text:
The Company, through its subsidiary Wilson-Davis, recognizes revenue in accordance with ASC 606, Revenue from Contracts with Customers . Revenue is recognized to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration expected to be received. The Company applies the five-step model under ASC 606: (i) identify the contract with a customer, (ii) identify the performance obligations in the contract, (iii) determine the transaction price, (iv) allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations, and (v) recognize revenue when (or as) each performance obligation is satisfied.

Brokerage Commissions. Wilson-Davis earns commissions from executing securities transactions for customers. The Company acts as an agent in these arrangements. Commission revenue is recognized on the trade date, which is the point in time when the performance obligation is satisfied, as the security is selected, the price is determined, the trade is executed, and the risks and rewards of ownership have transferred to/from the customer.

Mutual Fund Commissions. Wilson-Davis earns commissions from sales of mutual funds. The Company recognizes revenue at the point in time when the mutual fund is purchased by the customer and the performance obligation has been satisfied.

Other Transaction-Based Fees.

Adjustment to net income primarily consisted of net changes in fair value for various financial instruments as follows: (a) $1,704,499 income for the change in fair value of the warrant liabilities, (b) $11,106,000 income from change in the fair value of earnout liability, (c) $382,154 income in change in fair value of convertible note, (d) $103,185 income in change in fair value of long term seller notes, (e) $334,549 income related to the Tau Agreement as the company did not utilize the ELOC and does not intend to utilize it further, (f) $1,799,545 income from change in the fair value of the Winston & Strawn subscription agreement, (g) $99,693 income from change in the fair value of the Debenture, and (h) $63,696 income from change in the fair value of the sellers convertible notes.

net sales.heading: Revenue Recognition
net sales.text:
The Company, through its subsidiary AtlasClearing, recognizes revenue in accordance with ASC 606, Revenue from Contracts with Customers . Revenue is recognized to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration expected to be received. The Company applies the five-step model under ASC 606: (i) identify the contract with a customer, (ii) identify the performance obligations in the contract, (iii) determine the transaction price, (iv) allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations, and (v) recognize revenue when (or as) each performance obligation is satisfied.

Brokerage Commissions. AtlasClearing earns commissions from executing securities transactions for customers. The Company acts as an agent in these arrangements. Commission revenue is recognized on the trade date, which is the point in time when the performance obligation is satisfied, as the security is selected, the price is determined, the trade is executed, and the risks and rewards of ownership have transferred to/from the customer.

Mutual Fund Commissions. AtlasClearing earns commissions from sales of mutual funds. The Company recognizes revenue at the point in time when the mutual fund is purchased by the customer and the performance obligation has been satisfied.

Other Transaction-Based Fees.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: During the year ended June 30, 2026, revenues from commissions and related vetting fees accounted for approximately 46% and 7%, of total revenue, respectively.
During the year ended June 30, 2025, revenues from commissions and related vetting fees accounted for approximately 55% and 13%, of total revenue, respectively.
Revenues of $20,052,635 for the year ended June 30, 2026, represent a 85% increase from revenues of $10,856,612 for the year ended June 30, 2025.
Under applicable Federal Reserve Regulation T requirements, AtlasClearing is authorized to extend credit for up to 50% of the cost of new securities purchases.
AtlasClearing relies on its industry contacts and customer referrals to market its services.
In recruiting, training and retaining personnel, AtlasClearing relies on industry training and competitive compensation.
Our future success depends on our continuing ability to attract, train, assimilate, and retain highly skilled personnel.
We believe our future success depends upon our ability to attract and retain highly competent personnel.

Many of such companies have only recently been organized, have inadequate financial resources or liquidity and rely on the ongoing sale of stock or borrowings to sustain operations, do not have independent directors, and have engaged in material transactions with related parties.
Likewise, AtlasClearing relies upon financial and compliance professionals who are not registered representatives but who perform important services to the firm.
AtlasClearing’s business depends on its ability to execute large volumes of transactions for its own customers and to clear large volumes of transactions for introducing broker-dealers.
AtlasClearing relies on numerous external service providers whose failure to provide those services properly may result in significant adverse events.

AtlasClearing relies on numerous third-party service providers, including communication systems providers, regulatory services providers, clearing systems, exchange systems, banking systems, and market information providers.
AtlasClearing relies on representations of third parties to ensure compliance with applicable laws and rules.
In applying its compliance program, the firm relies on various customer and other third-party representations.
Similarly, in making a market in securities, AtlasClearing frequently relies on exemption from certain requirements that depend in part on conclusions of third parties.
We rely on sophisticated information technology (“IT”) systems and infrastructure to support our business.
AtlasClear Holdings relies on the third-party services of Pacsquare which may expose it to additional risks and could have an adverse impact on its business.

AtlasClear Holdings relies on the third-party services of Pacsquare to customize and integrate the AtlasClear Platform, source code and technology assets and to maintain the software it provides along with industry updates as needed.

Our continued eligibility to maintain the listing of our Common Stock on the NYSE American depends on a number of factors, including the price of our Common Stock and the number of persons that hold our Common Stock.

Any future determination to pay dividends will be at the discretion of our Board and will depend on our financial condition, results of operations, capital requirements, restrictions contained in the Stockholders’ Agreement and future agreements and financing instruments, business prospects and such other factors as our Board deems relevant.
We cannot predict whether investors will find securities issued by us less attractive because we elect to rely on these exemptions.
